# How to Teach ChatGPT Your Preferences So You Never Have to Repeat Yourself

Imagine walking into your favourite local café and having the barista hand over your exact coffee order without you saying a single word. You can actually get that same seamless experience with AI by using its memory feature to store your personal and professional preferences. 

Instead of typing your job title, dietary requirements, or writing style every single time you start a new conversation, you can teach the AI these details once, and it will remember them forever. 

## Understanding how AI memory works

Normally, when you start a new conversation with an AI, it begins with a completely blank slate. It forgets your previous discussions to keep your data secure and to manage its context window (the amount of text the AI can "remember" at one time during a single chat). 

With the memory feature enabled, the AI keeps a quiet, digital notepad in the background. When you share something useful about yourself, it automatically clips that detail and saves it. 

The next time you type a prompt (the instruction or question you give to the AI), it automatically reviews its notepad to make sure the response fits your life. 

## How to manage your AI's memory

You do not need to be a tech wizard to use this feature. In fact, you can set it up just by having a normal conversation. 

1. **Just say it**: You can directly tell the AI what to remember. For example, you can type: *"Remember that I write in Australian English and prefer concise summaries."* The AI will reply with a small notification saying "Memory updated".
2. **Let it learn naturally**: As you chat about your weekly meal prep or work projects, the AI will pick up on key details. If you mention that you have a golden retriever named Max, it might save that fact to help with future pet-care questions.
3. **Review and edit**: You are always in control of your data. If you move house, change jobs, or simply want to start fresh, you can manage these details easily. Go to your settings, look for the personalisation menu, and select "Manage Memory". Here, you will see a list of everything the AI knows about you, with a clear option to delete any detail with a single click. 

Think of this like a simple form of fine-tuning (the process of customising an AI model to follow a specific style or task) but without any of the complicated technical setup. 

## What this means for you

* **For your everyday life**: You can save hours on life organisation. Teach the AI your family’s dietary restrictions, the ingredients currently in your pantry, or your fitness goals. The next time you ask for a recipe, it will automatically exclude foods you dislike.
* **For your business or work**: You can maintain a consistent professional voice. Tell the AI your business's target audience, your specific role, and your preferred formatting rules. When you ask it to draft an email, it will sound like you, not a generic computer program.
* **If you're just getting started**: Keep it simple. Open a new chat today and type one basic preference, such as: *"Remember that I prefer metric measurements for all recipes."*

## Wrap-up

Teaching your AI assistant about your preferences turns a generic tool into a personalised partner that understands how you live and work. It takes the repetition out of your day so you can focus on getting things done. To get started today, open your chat app, head to the settings to ensure memory is toggled on, and tell the AI one thing that will make your next conversation just a little bit easier.
